correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary cases follow from the finite-projective-plane axioms: at order at least three all types of one- or two-sensor placement leave every observed vertex with zero or at least two unobserved neighbors, so propagation cannot start. At order two same-side/incident pairs fail and every antiflag succeeds by first forcing the three points off the selected line, then three other lines. Identification with the line graph of the 4-regular Fano nonincidence graph proves edge counts and adjacency restrictions. The two-coordinate cross-incidence metric proves a diameter of three and all four geodesic types; independently reconstructed Fano graph models reproduce 28 states, 84 jumps, 0 slides and distance/path-count profiles. The order-three enumeration is corroboration only.

value.rationale: Power domination with a fixed, very small sensor budget is a natural monitoring problem on point-line incidence networks. The plane axioms yield an exact universal two-sensor cutoff without assuming Desarguesian coordinates; the Fano boundary is fully classifiable and gives a nontrivial line-graph reconfiguration geometry, exact geodesics and a provable complete freezing under physically adjacent relocation. This structural separation provides a natural benchmark and cannot be obtained by simply substituting a parameter into a general reconfiguration formula. The narrow higher-order lower-bound claim is explicit and not overstated.
